text:
maria: heads-up — compliance asked for a clear plan on PII in spans/exporters. we currently let spans include user.email/user_id/raw_input. need options and tradeoffs.
sam: +1. main choices: redact at collector, encrypt sensitive fields with KMS, or pseudonymize (hash/tokenize) before export. each has pros/cons for debuggability and audit.
jordan: personally leaning to a layered approach: mark span attrs as `sensitive=true` and then allow per-org export policy: redact | pseudonymize | encrypt. makes routing decisions simpler.
lee: how would that `sensitive` flag get set? instrumentations won't always know. we should provide SDK helpers and an agent rule set. maybe default rules + allow app override.
maria: sketch of an exporter config we discussed:
```yaml
exporters:
  otlp:
    pii_strategy: encrypt   # one of: clear, redact, pseudonymize, encrypt
    kms_key: projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/telemetry/cryptoKeys/tel-key
    redact_patterns:
      - email
      - credit_card
``` 
sam: encrypt at collector + KMS avoids sending plaintext to downstream exporters but makes search/alerts harder (can’t index encrypted value). pseudonymize (reversible) helps audits but requires KMS/secret store + strict access logs.
tara: for audits we need ability to rehydrate (reversible token) under strict IAM + audited flow. also retention: legal wants 90 days for some fields, but product telemetry wants 14 days — need per-attr retention tiers.
jordan: agree. propose schema: span attrs get metadata: `sensitivity: low|medium|high`, `retention_days: N`, `export_allowed: true|false`. Collector enforces. keep defaults conservative.
maria: UX question for Console — how should teams pick strategy? add a per-project toggle under Project Settings -> Telemetry -> PII handling with presets (default conservative, dev-friendly, compliance). show expected downstream effects (search, cost, rehydration windows).
lee: implementation note: OTLP semantic conventions sometimes duplicate email in different attrs. we should add a normalization pass in the collector that tags common sensitive keys.
sam: also need audit logs for key usage + rehydration requests; tie into platform's KMS audit trail. security + compliance will need a playbook for who can request rehydrate and SLA for approval.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: telemetry-collector@staging v2.4.1 -> will include `pii_strategy` flag. changelog: https://redwood.internal/changelog/telemetry-2.4.1
tara: next steps: (1) define `sensitivity` enum + default rules (lee + jordan) (2) collector config prototype (maria) (3) console UX wires (tara) (4) compliance playbook draft (sam). can we aim for an RFC next week?
maria: yep. I'll create RFC skeleton and tag owners. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
